definition: In architecture and space planning, the space allocation problem (SAP) is the problem of assigning rooms and other spaces to positions, sizes and shapes within a building.
details: The resulting layout must usually satisfy requirements concerning room area, dimensions, adjacency, access, circulation and the location of doors, windows and building services. The problem is computationally difficult because even a small number of rooms can be arranged in many different ways. Space-allocation systems are therefore generally used to generate and compare possible layouts rather than to produce a single universally correct design. The subject overlaps with automated floor plan generation and with facility layout planning in industrial engineering, which is commonly formulated as a quadratic assignment problem. Facility-layout research often concentrates on the placement of departments or equipment, while architectural space allocation may also consider circulation, privacy, daylight, structure and building regulations.

explainer.lead: In architecture and space planning, the space allocation problem (SAP) is assigning rooms and other spaces to positions, sizes and shapes within a building. It is computationally hard, so systems compare candidate layouts rather than output one correct design.

tiers.eli5: It is the puzzle of fitting rooms of the right size and shape into a building while keeping the layout usable.
tiers.practitioner: Such systems generate and compare possible layouts, so treat output as options, not a single correct design. Even a few rooms give many arrangements, which is why exhaustive search does not scale.
tiers.paperLevel: The problem assigns rooms and spaces to positions, sizes and shapes subject to requirements on area, dimensions, adjacency, access, circulation, and door, window and building-service locations. It is computationally difficult because even a small number of rooms can be arranged in many ways; it overlaps with automated floor plan generation.

explainer.example: For a small building with a handful of rooms, a space-allocation system generates several layouts satisfying area and adjacency requirements so a designer can compare them.
